A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 11-page versions of the same AutoOcc paper, with matching methods, equations and experiments. Neither contains appendix pages or embedded supplementary files. v2 mentions separate supplementary material, whose contents are unavailable in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original occupancy-annotation experiments on Occ3D-nuScenes and SemanticKITTI, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark scores in Tables 2–3, efficiency measurements in Table 4 and ablations in Table 5.

M1.justification: Vision-language guidance, semantic-aware scalable Gaussians, self-estimated flow, LiDAR constraints and cumulative Gaussian-to-voxel splatting retain the same procedures. Removing the detailed VLM configuration from Section 4.1 does not establish a model replacement.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Occ3D-nuScenes occupancy annotation and SemanticKITTI cross-dataset, unseen-category generalization. Camera-only and multimodal coverage, dynamic objects, and difficult lighting/weather scenarios remain. Removing one displayed example does not establish changed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4 and Figure 4. Table 2 retains all seven baselines; Table 3 retains GaussianOcc, OVO, SurroundOcc and VLM-LiDAR. Citation renumbering and renaming 'Ours' to 'AutoOcc' do not change comparators.

E3.justification: Image resolutions, progressive resizing, optimizer settings and temporal aggregation remain unchanged. v3 explicitly excludes 'other' and 'other flat', consistent with v2's existing Table 2 categories and reported averages. Table 3's expanded training/evaluation description documents the retained cross-dataset experiment.

E4.justification: Figure 5 removes one of the two pole-reconstruction examples, reducing the displayed difficult-condition case studies from four to three. The remaining pole, rain and nighttime examples persist. SFM, SSG and LiDAR-loss ablations and the dynamic-object analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or other experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: One qualitative result is removed from Figure 5. Numerical results in Tables 2–5 are unchanged after matching reordered rows, including AutoOcc-V/M mIoU values of 20.92/25.84 on Occ3D-nuScenes and 9.36/12.76 on SemanticKITTI.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical definitions remain substantively unchanged. Minor notation and grammatical edits introduce no new assumptions, derivations, formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of automatic open-ended annotation, efficient VL-GS representation, dynamic-object handling and cross-dataset generalization remain. Although one contribution bullet drops 'or LiDAR', vision-only capability and comparative performance remain explicit elsewhere.

C2.justification: Figure 4's caption is shortened, but its human-comparison and baseline-performance interpretations remain in Section 4.2. Explanations concerning geometric priors, dynamic trailing, weather robustness and generalization remain substantively unchanged. No new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 removes the CogVLM-17B, EVA2-CLIP-E and Vicuna-7B-v1.5 configuration and the CLIP-based category-mapping description. v3 adds eight A100 GPUs, explicit class exclusions and clearer cross-dataset documentation. The abstract's planned code/model release statement is removed; actual resource availability cannot be determined from either PDF.

R1.justification: References to Vicuna, CLIP, EVA-CLIP and CogVLM are removed alongside the implementation passage. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against occupancy-annotation, reconstruction and open-world methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical corrections, revises contribution and caption wording, adds acknowledgments and removes the supplementary-material pointer. The main section sequence and narrative organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive label and diagram edits. Figure 5 changes from four examples arranged in two rows to three in one row. Table 3 loses class-color swatches, Table 5 reorders ablation rows, and several figures and tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 improves some wording, diagrams and evaluation documentation, and discloses hardware. However, removing the VLM configuration and CLIP category-mapping procedure from Section 4.1 makes the central experiments harder to reproduce. With the quantitative evidence unchanged, these losses in technical transparency outweigh the limited presentation gains.
